title: Research note (no κ): T74 #2322 words pay 525 rank units/call of end-of-call restoration climbs — each more cold-restored helper worth +0.6–1.5e-6 (LP ceiling); buffers are free in κ
body:
**Research note (pricing screen); no κ claim.** This note finds and prices the largest remaining item of pure restoration work on the live T74 line: the end-of-call climbs to FULL that FULL-cleanup helpers make only so the inverse-reverse cleanup can run at FULL. The object is the #2322 words, which the open #2349 / #2363 / #2374 line builds on.

| item (both providers, per call) | value |
|---|---|
| FULL-cleanup / cold-restored (hyperplane-ended) helpers | 356 / 78 |
| end climbs paid by FULL-cleanup helpers | {1:249, 2:42, 3:64}: **525 rank units, 9.8% of local paid mass (5,371)** |
| end climbs paid by cold-restored helpers | none |
| **one more cold-restored helper**, end climb 1 / 2 / 3 | **+5.77e-7 / +1.04e-6 / +1.46e-6** in the LP ceiling b |
| all 249 / 42 / 64 of one class | +6.31% / +2.33% / +4.00% |
| ideal, all 355 | LP ceiling 0.0018806 (+10.8%; an upper bound for the lever, not achievable as stated) |

For comparison (#2402): on the same words a #2322-type handoff is worth +4.27e-8, and all remaining owner-fill headroom is at most 8.1e-10.

**Buffers are free; legality is the obstacle.** These facts are read from #2374's pinned SPEC, OUTER-CLAIM and invoice:
- κ = C − 1/F − B with F = 1e3046 and B = 1e-3022. Zero buffers, CLEARs and adapters therefore enter only through admission inequalities, which have huge slack.
- Physical stock would go 66,826 → 67,181, against a parent capacity of 112,178.
- #2322's namespace bound NZ ≤ R becomes 433 ≤ 434.

So the open obligation is whether each helper's cleanup can legally move before its end climb. The existing hyperplane-ended helpers come from #601's sufficient commutation test and #604/#617-style cold tails. Cold ends are a well-known move class on older words (#636, #640, #676, #685, credited). This note prices it on the live line; the prices are what a stronger exact commutation test, or a changed cleanup contract, would be worth. #1995/#2013 hold the cleanup contract fixed, so this lies outside their scope.

**Checks.**
- `restoration_prices.py` recounts both pinned #2322 words, using the vendored #2387 frame-climb rule patched only to label which register and phase pays each child. Each recount matches the word's reported profile.
- Prices come from the width-aware bin-pattern LP of #2387 / #2360 (pattern dual of #1129), extended to widths 3–9. As a control, the extended LP reproduces the #2322 ceiling.
- A separate AI subagent wrote its own GF(2) replay from a plain rule statement and agreed on every census number in both providers.
- `--check-only`, the 3.10 grammar check and the research tests pass. Everything ran on CPython 3.14.4; the registered 3.12 replay was not run.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/t74-restoration-climb-prices/restoration_prices.py --fetch   # ~2.5 min
# PASS_T74_RESTORATION_PRICES full_cleanup=356 end_climb_mass=525 convertible=355 one_d1=+5.767e-07 one_d3=+1.463e-06 ideal=+10.80% no_new_kappa
```

**Scope.**
- No conversion is constructed or shown legal.
- Prices are LP-ceiling differences on the fixed bin stock.
- They assume an earlier cleanup changes no other register's climbs. #601 records that intervening partner climbs stay paid; #604-type tails would have to be priced on the actual word.
- Base: main `0fdd7d82`. Assignment: recursive-interfaces track (seed 55, "eliminate restoration work"). Card: `complex-new-helper-inventory`, scope changed, with the reason in TASK.json.

**Open next questions.**
- An exact commutation test over the 355 helpers, starting with the 64 end-climb-3 helpers.
- A #604-style cold tail on one helper, priced on the recounted word.
- The same census on the selected k8 word's 402 FULL-cleanup helpers.
